description: RAIN assembles a daily operational picture across EMS dispatch, NEMT logs, the telehealth demand queue, facility capacity, the risk engine, and the weather feed — surfacing transport backlogs, telehealth demand surges, and EMS coverage gaps before you ask, on the device you carry in the field.

Identifies friction in rural care delivery that no single operational system shows: the 8-to-11 a.m. corridor collision between prenatal and dialysis transports, EMS/NEMT double-bookings from unshared queues, and the vehicle bottleneck driving both delays.
Forecasts how converting eligible trips to telehealth frees vehicles and crews, projecting the downstream effect on the queue overflow and on EMS response time across the frontier service area.

Generates a consolidated transport schedule, telehealth conversions, EMS crew reassignment, and a daily risk panel — published to dispatch and cached offline to field devices for the corridor's connectivity dead zones.
